newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Africans seek trigger price for coffee export cut.
newsitem.headline: Africans seek trigger price for coffee export cut.

text.p: African nations are to propose trigger prices in a scheme to cut exports by members of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) in the first half of this year, said Ivorian Minister for Commodities Guy-Alain Gauze.
"It is a very sophisticated scheme," Gauze said at an international seminar in Rio de Janeiro.
There would be separate trigger prices for arabica and robusta coffee similar to a scheme earlier implemented by the ACPC, Gauze added.
"We are just working now on the prices," he said.

The plan would be discussed later today with other members of the ACPC. African producers called for a full meeting of the ACPC to discuss a proposed 2.5 million bag reduction in member exports during January to June 1997.
In a speech to delegates, Gauze said that an abundance of supply between July 1996 and June 1997, as well as the just-in-time buying strategy of the roasters, had "strongly depressed the market."
Between July and December 1996, the composite indicative coffee price had lost 14.62 percent. The robusta indicative price had shown an even greater loss of 20.42 percent.
As well, option strategies on the part of European and North American funds to liquidate their long positions have put more pressure on the market.

The prices recently recovered on predictions for a lower 1997/98 Brazilian crop, encouraging signs from Vietnam with regard to membership of the ACPC, a reinforcement of the coffee export limitation program and the return of investment funds trying to buy back their short positions.

"We should not let ourselves get heady because of the recent improvement in the market...because we need courageous initiatives and consolidating moves so that the recent improvement in prices doesn't appear to be a phenomenon which precedes a reversal in prices," Gauze said.
